item.title: Palm Springs Man Appears in Court for DUI Hit-and-Run Murder of 14-Year-Old Liam Cantu
item.description: Earlier this morning, Jose Villegas Orbe, the Palm Springs man charged in the DUI hit-and-run murder of a 14-year-old boy, appeared once again at the Indio Larson Justice Center for a felony settlement conference.The victim was identified as Liam Cantu, a freshman at La Quinta High School. Liam’s parents, Jesus Cantu and Jennifer Perez, were present at the hearing, facing the man accused of killing their son for the first time since the deadly crash last year. item.title: Low-Cost Spay and Neuter Services Expanding in East Valley Through Mobile Clinics
item.description: Pet owners in the East Valley will soon have greater access to affordable spay and neuter services through new mobile clinics provided by the Riverside County Department of Animal Services.The county says the mobile units will bring critical veterinary services directly into local communities, making it easier for residents to care for their pets and prevent unwanted litters. item.title: Cathedral City Considers Andrew Firestine for City Manager Role
item.description: Cathedral City officials are considering appointing Andrew Firestine as the city’s next city manager.The proposed appointment was announced today and will be reviewed at the City Council meeting scheduled for February 11.If approved, Firestine would replace former City Manager Charlie McClendon, who retired last September. item.title: Supreme Court Clears California’s New Congressional Map for Midterm Elections
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court has cleared the way for California to use its newly approved congressional map in this year’s midterm elections.The ruling was issued in a brief, one-sentence order and included no explanation or noted dissents. item.title: La Quinta Shoe Drive Collects Gently Used Footwear to Help Families and the Environment
item.description: The City of La Quinta is partnering with the nonprofit Friends of the Desert Mountains to launch a community shoe drive aimed at helping families in need while promoting environmental sustainability. The drive began on the first of the month and runs through March 31, giving residents several weeks to donate gently used footwear.Organizers say nearly any type of wearable shoe is welcome, including sandals, sneakers, dress shoes, and snow boots. item.title: Hideaway Golf Club Raises Thousands to Help Fight Hunger in the Coachella Valley
item.description: Members of the Hideaway Golf Club in La Quinta are making a major impact in the fight against hunger across the Coachella Valley. item.title: La Quinta Kicks Off Free “Concerts in the Park” Series at SilverRock
item.description: The sun may have set in La Quinta, but the entertainment is just getting started as the city launches this year’s Concerts in the Park series.
